title: Groups of Shifted Words

concept.title: The pattern of differences as a key
body: Shifting a word means adding the same number to every letter, wrapping around from `z` to `a`: `abc` becomes `bcd`, and `xyz` becomes `yza`. What does **not** change under a shift is the difference between neighbouring letters (taken modulo 26). So the list of these differences is a canonical key of the group.

body.code: key = tuple((ord(w[i + 1]) - ord(w[i])) % 26 for i in range(len(w) - 1))

body: Words of different length have keys of different length, so they never share a group. A one-letter word has the empty key: all one-letter words are shifts of each other.

statement: Two words are in the same group if one can be turned into the other by shifting every letter forward by the same number of places in the alphabet (after `z` comes `a`). Words of different length are never in the same group. Given `n` words, print the number of groups, and then the sizes of the groups from the largest to the smallest.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` words.
outputFormat: The first line: the number of groups.
The second line: the sizes in decreasing order.
constraints: Each word has 1 to 10 lowercase letters.

examples.input:
6
abc bcd acef xyz az ba

hints: What stays the same when every letter is shifted by the same amount?
The differences between neighbouring letters (modulo 26) form a key.
Count how many words share each key and sort the counts.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
w = input().split()

# Your code here

explanation: Shifts keep the differences of neighbouring letters (modulo 26), so the difference list identifies the group.
solution.complexity: Time O(total length), space O(total length).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
w = input().split()

groups = {}
for word in w:
    key = tuple((ord(word[i + 1]) - ord(word[i])) % 26 for i in range(len(word) - 1))
    groups[key] = groups.get(key, 0) + 1
sizes = sorted(groups.values(), reverse=True)
print(len(sizes))
print(*sizes)
